source: NASA/GSFC Five Millennium Catalog of Solar and Lunar Eclipses (Espenak & Meeus)
note: Times are the instant of greatest eclipse in UTC.

eclipses.regions: Southern Chile, Argentina, Angola, Zambia
eclipses.notes: A narrow ring of fire crossed the South Atlantic between South America and Africa.

eclipses.regions: Continental United States, coast to coast
eclipses.notes: The "Great American Eclipse": the first totality to span the contiguous US since 1918.

eclipses.regions: Asia, Australia, the Pacific and western North America
eclipses.notes: Widely billed as a "super blue blood Moon" — a second full Moon of the month near perigee.

eclipses.regions: South America, Europe, Africa, Asia and Australia
eclipses.notes: The longest total lunar eclipse of the 21st century; Mars was at opposition the same week.

eclipses.regions: The Americas, Europe and western Africa
eclipses.notes: A high, well-placed totality for observers on both sides of the Atlantic.

eclipses.regions: South Pacific, Chile and Argentina
eclipses.notes: Totality passed over the observatories of the Chilean Atacama near sunset.

eclipses.regions: Saudi Arabia, southern India, Sumatra and Borneo
eclipses.notes: A bright ring of fire seen at sunrise from the Arabian peninsula.

eclipses.regions: Central Africa, northern India, China and Taiwan
eclipses.notes: An extremely thin annulus on the day of the June solstice.

eclipses.regions: Chile and Argentina (Patagonia), southern Pacific and Atlantic
eclipses.notes: Totality crossed the Araucanía region of Chile and Río Negro in Argentina.

eclipses.regions: The Pacific, Australia, eastern Asia and western Americas
eclipses.notes: A very short totality with the Moon close to perigee.

eclipses.regions: Northern Canada, Greenland and Arctic Russia
eclipses.notes: A high-Arctic ring of fire; a partial eclipse rose over eastern North America.

eclipses.regions: The Americas, the Pacific, eastern Asia and Australia
eclipses.notes: A near-total partial eclipse, and the longest partial lunar eclipse in centuries.

eclipses.regions: Antarctica and the Southern Ocean
eclipses.notes: Only expedition camps and flights over Antarctica saw totality.

eclipses.regions: The Americas, Europe and Africa
eclipses.notes: A deep, dark totality well placed for the Atlantic-facing continents.

eclipses.regions: Asia, Australia, the Pacific and the Americas
eclipses.notes: The last total lunar eclipse before a three-year gap.

eclipses.duration: up to 86% of the Sun covered
eclipses.regions: Europe, north-east Africa, the Middle East and western Asia
eclipses.notes: A large partial eclipse best seen from western Siberia.

eclipses.regions: Western Australia, East Timor and West Papua
eclipses.notes: A rare hybrid eclipse that shifted between annular and total along its track.

eclipses.regions: Western United States, Central America, Colombia and Brazil
eclipses.notes: A ring of fire from Oregon to the Yucatán and on into South America.

eclipses.regions: Europe, Africa, Asia and Australia
eclipses.notes: A shallow bite out of the Moon's northern limb.

eclipses.regions: Mexico, the United States from Texas to Maine, and eastern Canada
eclipses.notes: A long totality near solar maximum, with a bright, structured corona.

eclipses.regions: The Americas, Europe and Africa
eclipses.notes: A small partial eclipse of a supermoon.

eclipses.regions: Easter Island, southern Chile and Argentina
eclipses.notes: One of the longest annular phases of the decade, mostly over open ocean.

eclipses.regions: The Americas, the Pacific and western Europe
eclipses.notes: The first total lunar eclipse since November 2022.

eclipses.duration: up to 94% of the Sun covered
eclipses.regions: North-eastern North America, Europe, north-west Africa and the Arctic
eclipses.notes: A deeply partial sunrise eclipse for eastern Canada.

eclipses.regions: Europe, Africa, Asia and Australia
eclipses.notes: A long, deep totality superbly placed for observers across Asia.

eclipses.duration: up to 86% of the Sun covered
eclipses.regions: New Zealand, the South Pacific and Antarctica
eclipses.notes: A far-southern partial eclipse on the eve of the September equinox.

eclipses.regions: Antarctica, with partial phases across southern Africa and South America
eclipses.notes: A ring of fire over the ice of East Antarctica.

eclipses.regions: Eastern Asia, Australia, the Pacific and the Americas
eclipses.notes: Totality straddled the Pacific, with moonset shading the eclipse in Asia.

eclipses.regions: Greenland, Iceland and northern Spain
eclipses.notes: The first totality over mainland Europe since 1999, seen low in the evening sky from Spain.

eclipses.regions: The Americas, Europe and Africa
eclipses.notes: A deep partial eclipse that leaves only a sliver of the Moon in sunlight.

eclipses.regions: Chile, Argentina and the South Atlantic
eclipses.notes: A very long ring of fire crossing Patagonia.

eclipses.regions: The Americas, Europe and Africa
eclipses.notes: A subtle shading of the Moon's disc rather than a visible bite.

eclipses.regions: Southern Spain, Morocco, Algeria, Libya, Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Yemen
eclipses.notes: The longest totality on land this century so far, with the track crossing Luxor.

eclipses.regions: The Americas, Europe and Africa
eclipses.notes: A grazing partial eclipse of the Moon's northern limb.

eclipses.regions: Ecuador, Peru, Brazil, Suriname, Portugal and Spain
eclipses.notes: One of the longest annular eclipses of the century, ending at sunset over Iberia.

eclipses.regions: Western and eastern Australia (including Sydney) and New Zealand
eclipses.notes: Totality passes directly over Sydney harbour for the first time since 1857.

eclipses.regions: Europe, Africa, Asia and Australia
eclipses.notes: A New Year's Eve totality for the eastern hemisphere.

eclipses.regions: The Americas, Europe and Africa
eclipses.notes: A central passage through Earth's shadow — one of the darkest eclipses of the century.

eclipses.regions: The Americas, Europe, Africa and western Asia
eclipses.notes: A long winter night totality for the Atlantic-facing continents.

eclipses.regions: Algeria, Greece, Turkey, Russia, northern China and Japan
eclipses.notes: A ring of fire that sweeps from the Mediterranean to Hokkaido.

eclipses.regions: Botswana, South Africa and southern Australia
eclipses.notes: Totality crosses the Kalahari and later the coast near Adelaide.

eclipses.regions: The Americas, Europe, Africa and western Asia
eclipses.notes: A shallow but unmistakable totality closing out the decade.
